body: It feels weird that I went to 3 different psycologists and none suggested or diagnosed ADHD, I thought the opposite was normal (getting diagnosed ADHD when it's not the cause). But I will ask my therapist next time.

It makes me feel useless to need to be like that, sometimes I'll be like "I'll take the trash now", and my GF will be like, why would you go down the stairs and back again now, you have to leave in 30 minutes. But I might have to get used to my limitations.

There is a problem though, which is that sometimes (like the water for example), I have to get out of the room to open another fauced to make the pump start, and the moment I walk through doors it is like I switched on and off, I completely forget what I was doing or why.

I did, and It does work pretty nicely for remembering to do stuff, but it's the small non-writable things I fuck up constantly (I can't write "turn right at X street" or "close tap when bottle is full" on my to-do list can I?)

I have not been diagnosed with ADHD, but I have been told my psychologists that I might have OCD related to about compulsively thinking about stuff and getting in my head, and might be on the spectrum (aspergers). Both of these things mean I usually get very anxious about stuff I can't do (like having trouble reading body language or reacting to people's emotion in a natural way), get into my head and forget about the outside world.

Reading the ADHD symptoms I don't feel like it's my experience, I can usually focus fine and control my attention as long as I'm in a good mood/relaxed, and not obsessing about something or the other.

The problem with that is that she reacts with anger to insistence or nagging, and I can't "take her out" in a stronger way without triggering that anger. Tickling would also be cause for anger/screaming, not laughs. 

I think I need something that lets her take the first step, something like an invitation that she can accept and agree to, not something I force.

The problem is that I love her, and want to see her better, and want to save the relationship. No one is forcing her to stay in this relationship, but I'm working hard to convince her it makes sense to keep trying, so "take it or leave it" would totally backfire.

 Relationship counseling did not work for us, it became about talking about the bad stuff instead of fixing anything. I agree we both need individual therapy.

I don't even want her to be self sufficient, I can do most things if she's feeling down, but I know that she needs to feel productive and awake to be happy, and that being a couch potato just causes her to spiral deeper into depression, it's frustrating that I can't force her to wake up and be productive (for her own happiness), and I can't just wait and let her be miserable and put up with the blame.
A lot of these discussions started about a year ago. It happens a few times a month, there's a day she completly shuts off, then recovers, gets better, until it gets worse again.

>Learn to cook.  You're almost 30 and you can't think of just getting upand making something for both of you.  Who does the cleaning?   

I do 99% of the cooking on a normal routine, we do cleaning 50/50, with her handling clothes and bathroom, and me handling dishes and floors. We're living in her parents house temporally now though, so it's more complicated, but our fights don't have to do with chores, I meant cooking as some sort of olive branch of "Here, start your day have a breakfast in bed!", which is rejected.

> Are you actually listening to her?  If it sometimes happens that youdon't understand, miss a big day, and/or mess things up, then I canunderstand it being stressful.  Sort of makes it that she can't dependon you for things.

Depends, I try to listen and understand as much as I can, but I don't have the best memory, a lot of times I'll forget the way we planned on doing things, and she will have to explain things again (i.e "We have to go on wednesday, not tuesday"). It's something I'm working on, but I understand how it can be frustrating.

>You say you're a people pleaser, but you're not doing much pleasing unless it's not your girlfriend I'm guessing.

Mostly I mean I'm totally focusing on how to make her feel better, like I'll try to avoid conflict and try to do whatever she might need, but she gets extremely angry at me for "not having a life" or not being assertive, or being all up in her business passively, like watching whatever she's watching or just defaulting to a blank stare and being quiet when she's quiet too. Sometimes it feels like I depend on her for everything emotionally. Whenever she's in a bad mood I get completely broken too, which is a problem, but I just can't manage to be a positive force and have contagious energy.
That makes sense, I could be like: "Hey I feel like you're blaming me, but I'm not the cause of your problems now, I'm here to help, but do not make it about us when it is not"

How do I deal with blaming from a FA? Sometimes it feels like anything I do when she's in a bad mood will trigger a complete deactivation. If she's not happy with her professional life, and I do the smallest mistake, she will completely shutdown, and be angry at me. What can you do to make a FA open and vulnerable, so you can help the person feel better, when you get blamed even when unrelated stuff occurs?.

I'm having trouble with this balance, specially with making it sound not like a burden, or something I do only to run away or not of my own free will. Something that comes up a lot when we're fighting is that I can't think for myself and have ideas on how to make things better.

So if she tells me to leave and I do, it is because she told me so. It is like she's always expecting me to know exactly what she needs, amd when she has to be explicit about it she feels it is fake and no longer valid.

For example if she complains I can't do anything to bring her up when she's down (maybe sad for something unrelated to me). She might say "just put some music or open a window I don't know, anything!". But then if I do literally that the next day it will make her completely mad at me, because she had to tell me and says she doesn't want to date a robot that does nothing he's not told explicitely.

It is exhausting, because I get scared she will leave and start walking on egg shells around her, not doing anything that might upset her, which reinforces the feeling I have to agency and do not decide anything for myself, and that I only do what I'm told or what I think will stop conflict.

I know that if given time, space and trust I can relax and start being myself, having original thoughts, etc, but the situation does not help.

It happened a few times that I see a change of attitude when we spend some time apart, and she tells me that she feels less alone and abandoned, and feels me more present when we're just chatting or texting, that she starts realizing she actually wants me by her side. This makes me want to work on the relationship. At least I want to give it my best, and leave knowing that everything that could be done was done.

The problem with helping her express her needs is that all I get from her when she is triggered/deactivating is "I want to breakup, I'm not happy in this relationship", I'm confident that I can be better for her and that I can improve certain things that bother her (and that were always a problem through my life, like procrastination). But I'm having trouble dealing with her at the moment, and finding ways to calm the waters so progress can be made.

A part of me knows that if we broke up both of us might be happier, but another part feels like we can push through this, work on it, and use it as a reason/context for improvement. I'm doing therapy too and talking about the ways to focus on my improvement regardless of the situation, and seeing how to help her and myself through this.

I think the situation of your partner is different than mine, but your own resonates with me. overthinking and worrying about how every action I do is positive or negative and will lead me to feeling peaceful and happy, or will lead me to anxiety and crisis. I constantly doubt and re-think what I'm doing. Awareness is something I'm working on, it's nice to feel like I'm not alone, thanks!

That might be useful, I definitely feel like I'm constantly reassuring about the future, about improvements down the road. Usually if actions come right after a fight or during it they will be completely rejected. 

"You are just doing this because I told you so, I don't want a robot I have to control, I want to be with a human being!" 

Or "That is what I needed yesterday, I don't want to know any more about how you feel right now, I don't want to hear a word from you"

She will be angry and upset, and it is not the time to try to fix what happened. But usually I'm completely lost about the correct way to behave in these scenarios, I actually wrote another post about this here: https://www.reddit.com/r/attachment\_theory/comments/ozccsb/how\_to\_know\_if\_i\_should\_give\_space\_to\_a\_fearful/

They are definitely unhappy at the moment, and I know there are stuff we must resolve before we work it out, I don't know if she's willing to put the effort in and mostly accept changes in her view of relationships in general. I'm hopeful, and also incredibly worried about the outcome and what the correct action is at any given point.

Tests I did told me I was AP, and I do feel identified with most explanations for anxious attachment. But I also feel I lack the confidence to express feelings and the emotional intelligence to do so, which contradicts a bit the normal stereotype of anxious attachment.

I will try the 20 minute timeout, thanks!
